criteria.name: artwork_craft
criteria.why: The cover (1) is a real image. It shows the vise and the part with two shadowed pockets, the end mill held clear, a dark spindle head under the type and a median L* of 12.3. Frame 6 is the hardest frame: 24 cyan-taped empty pads beside the 100 roofs at the same pitch, and the argument reads at 432 px. Frame 9 puts a worker in the bays with Lockheed's lit enclosures beyond them, and it works. More than one frame leans on a default, though. Frame 3 is 312 identical tiny pockets that read as a grille or keyboard texture at 432 px. The lifted 'unit' part is about 55 px wide in the 1600 display and has no focal pull, so the plan's own risk ('312 small parts can read as a texture') came true. Frame 8, the turn, has a primitive pendant: a rounded slab, a black rectangle and 36 beige calculator keys on a flat navy mid-tone panel. It is not the planned graphite falling to black, and the keys run under the footer. Frame 2 is a mid-grey tile grid that reads as graph paper, and the carpet's 'rolled corner' is a thin fold that barely casts. Frame 7 is a flat top-down blue sheet with the part shot straight down as a 2D icon, and machine_qa warns that its lower zone is dead (bands 0.35/0.07/0.15). Frame 4's two rows read as a server aisle. Its floor pool lands on empty aisle, not on the subject, and the worker is a stiff kit figure. Frame 1's chips are flat C-rings. That is under the 7 descriptor, which allows one weak frame, and well above the 4.

criteria.name: deck_coherence
criteria.why: The deck holds as one dark register, and the median L* audited on 1/6/9 is 12.3, 1.7 and 8.2. One accent, comal lit, means one thing (the cell) on 6, 7 and 9 only. The 5 to 6 hold is a real filmstrip device: identical roofs, with the 24 bays added across the aisle. The part motif runs 1 (vise), 3 (tray), 7 (on its drawing) and 9 (absent), and the casts come from the left throughout. It slips outside the world on 7 and 8. Frame 8's flat navy back panel and frame 7's cyanotype bring a cool blue mid-tone the warm lastLight shop never sets up. Frame 4's blue-lit enclosures read as a different room from 1's warm brown machine. Clearly one deck, with continuity devices doing real work and one or two frames outside it.

criteria.name: claim_integrity
criteria.why: Every numeral on the slides and in the caption traces to figures.json and a claim: 24/2027 (c4), 735,000/100,000/85,000/$300 million (c1, c2), 250,000/800/2025 (c12), 30 (c10), 100/2026 (c11), 2,000 (c5) and October 14th (c6). The scoping is careful. The 24 are kept apart from the nearly 100 on 6. The 2,000 is labelled statewide and company-own and never set against the 800. Dallas County comes from TDLR c34, not the release. AI is attributed only to Hadrian's description of its own factories, and the drawn 312 and 100 are disclosed as 'about' and 'draws 100'. Three small looseness points. The frame 1 hook says 'due in 2027' where c4 says 'expected to be operational in early 2027', though the dek restores it. On frame 7, the attribution 'Hadrian, on its own factories' is the claim-writer's gloss on a homepage line about Opus. The caption's 'Hadrian calls its own factories AI powered' leans on c24's wording, but c24's source (hadrian.co/blog/series-c) is not in the first comment, and c15 says 'combine ... AI' rather than 'AI powered'. All sources are first party, and those are the primary sources for this story.

criteria.name: story_and_stakes
criteria.why: A reader learns what happened (a 24-machine Hadrian cell plus a $300 million expansion), who decided (Lockheed Martin, with Hadrian), where (Grand Prairie, Dallas County) and when (expected early 2027, run by Lockheed's own workforce, frame 9). The stake is stated generally. The AI question on 8 ('Will AI do anything here?') is the point for this docket, but it is an open question with no consequence attached. Nothing tells a Texan what they can do next: there is no hiring route for the 2,000 jobs and no public proceeding, and the deck doesn't say none exists.

criteria.name: sequence_and_momentum
criteria.why: The cover hook 'A 24 machine cell, due in 2027' is clear but not urgent. Frames 2 to 5 are four consecutive scale-of-plant frames (area, parts, 30 machines, 100 machines). Frame 2 or 3 could move or go without loss. The AI thread, which is why this docket carries the story, doesn't arrive until 7. The turn at 6 is real and declared, the empty bays against the full block. Frame 9 lands on who runs it, with the bays still empty.

criteria.name: voice
criteria.why: Clean, plain and on register: 'These are Lockheed's own, not Hadrian's cell.' 'Lockheed's own crews will run it.' The caption's 'The release gives AI no job description' is a good line. Several deks narrate the method rather than the place: 'Each area is drawn as a square at one scale, not the plant's shape.' 'The block draws 100, at one scale.' Grand Prairie and Dallas County are named, but nothing in the copy sounds like someone who knows the Great Southwest industrial district. It is honest, without boosterism and without doom.

criteria.name: variety
criteria.why: The machine-shop world and the aluminium/graphite vocabulary are new against nos. 53 to 55. The structural moves are not. No. 54 set '80 boxes in a 100 slot block beside the projected plant's 300 slots at the same pitch', and no. 55 drew '25 lids in 41 taped bays'. Frames 5, 6 and 9 repeat both moves: a counted block beside a second block at the same pitch, and taped empty bays. The instrument is again a corporate release, and the caption again opens on what a document doesn't say, the absence spine earlier ledger entries asked runs to stop leaning on.

one_sentence_fix: Rebuild frame 8, the deck's turn, as the chassis pendant at full detail in a graphite enclosure falling to true black with the low west key raking the keys from the left, then recompose frame 3 as an oblique raking close so the lifted part reads as the unit before the 312 read as a texture.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: The turn frame's subject is a primitive model: a rounded slab, a black rectangle and 36 beige calculator keys. It sits on a flat navy mid-tone back panel instead of the planned graphite falling to black, there is no raking light on the keys, and the bottom key rows and knob run under the footer type.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Model the pendant at full detail: bevel, e-stop mushroom, MPG handwheel, feed/spindle override knobs and a glass screen with a seam reflection. Replace the navy panel with the graphite enclosure and shut door falling to black, light the keys' west edges with the low warm key, and crop so the housing fills about half the frame above the footer.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: In the straight-down plan, 312 identical pockets read as a grille or keyboard texture at 432 px. The lifted unit part is about 75 px wide at full size and has no focal pull, and the second tray fades into a dead grey lower band.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Tilt to an oblique raking view from the tray's near corner so the 13 rows of 24 run back toward a vanishing point. Put the empty pocket and the lifted part in the foreground at 300 px or more, with a long cast across the steel, and drop the second tray.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: A uniform mid-grey tile grid over the whole slab reads as graph paper and sits in the grey middle. The carpet's 'rolled corner' is a thin fold with almost no height or cast, so the relief reads as a flat diagram.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Drop the slab to near-black sealed concrete with only a few saw cuts and a raking key that shows its texture. Model the carpet corner as a real rolled cylinder 30 to 40 px high casting a long shadow to the right, and stand the form boards proud on the pour so they cast.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: The camera looks straight down at a flat blue sheet, so the part reads as a 2D icon with a drop shadow. The cyanotype lifts the frame into a cool mid-tone, and machine_qa flags a weak lower zone.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Move the camera to about 35 degrees oblique so the part stands on its plan view with its pocket walls and bosses visible in depth, casting long across the sheet. Deepen the cyanotype toward a near-black blue and let the sheet's edge and the granite fill the lower third.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: The two rows of enclosures with lit blue panels read as a server or data hall aisle. The floor pool lands on empty aisle rather than on the near machine and machinist, and no part or spindle tells you these are mills.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Light the near right-hand machine's window from inside with a lit part visible in its vise. Move the aisle pool onto the machinist and that machine, and add chip conveyors and coolant tanks at the machine bases so the rows read as machining centres.
